config.theme: Sprint planning for a payments team at a fictional fintech
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Sprint planning for a payments team at a fictional fintech

personas.name: Sofia
personas.goals: A realistic sprint the team can actually finish
personas.hidden_agenda: Her director already promised the refund API to the partner

personas.name: Marcus
personas.goals: Get the ledger refactor into the sprint

personas.name: Aiko
personas.goals: Refund API first, everything else second
catchphrases: from a product point of view

personas.name: Diego
personas.role: Junior engineer, newest on the team
personas.goals: Be useful, not be the reason anything slips
personas.hidden_agenda: Doesn't fully understand the bank certification

agenda.title: Carryover from last sprint
agenda.goal: Decide what rolls over and why it slipped

agenda.title: Capacity and estimates
agenda.goal: Match the plan to the people actually available

agenda.title: Risks and dependencies
agenda.goal: Name the risks and who is watching each one

facts.statement: Average velocity over the last 3 sprints = 38 points
Tickets carried over from last sprint = 5
Refund API committed date to the partner = November 4
Test coverage on the payments service = 72%

beats.summary: What slipped and why; Marcus inflates last sprint's velocity
Refund API vs bank certification vs the ledger refactor; Aiko misstates the deadline, nobody catches it
Who is actually around; PTO and on-call; an aside about the office plant becomes a whole thing
Security findings, the bank, the date; one owner, one non-owner, a dodged question

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Okay, team, sprint twenty-three. Let's start with what we didn't finish.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Realistically, most of it was the reconciliation job. It ate the second week.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: How many tickets are rolling over?

turns.speaker: Diego
turns.text: Five. Three of them are the reconciliation ones.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: And the other two are mine, the refund status page and the email template.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Look, we still did forty points, which is pretty good given the incident.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Forty sounds high to me. I'd want to check the board before we celebrate.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: From a product point of view I don't care about points, I care about the refund API.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Points are how we know if the refund API is even possible.

turns.speaker: Diego
turns.text: Sorry, quick one, does carryover count against this sprint's points or last sprint's?

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: It's re-estimated and counted in this sprint, that's how we've always done it.

turns.speaker: Diego
turns.text: Okay, cool. Thanks.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: The reconciliation job slipped because the bank sandbox was down for two days. That's not on us.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: It's not on anyone, it's just the reality of working with banks.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Let's be honest, though, we also started it late.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Fair.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Do the reconciliation tickets need re-estimating, or are the old numbers still good?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: They're still good. Most of the hard part is done, it's testing now.

turns.speaker: Diego
turns.text: I can help with the testing, if that's useful.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Let's figure out who's on what in capacity. Hold that.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: The template ticket can probably drop, honestly. Marketing hasn't even sent copy.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Is that a drop, or a not-yet?

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: A not-yet. Let's keep it in the backlog.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Okay. Then the reconciliation tickets and the status page roll over, and the template goes back to the backlog. That's settled.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Works for me.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Priorities. Aiko, you want to frame it?

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: Refund API, then the bank certification, then whatever's left. The partner is expecting refunds on November fourteenth.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And the ledger refactor?

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: The ledger refactor is invisible to customers.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: It's invisible until the ledger breaks. Then it's very visible.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: How long is the certification window with the bank?

turns.speaker: Diego
turns.text: Three weeks, I think. That's what the email said.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Three weeks, but the first week is usually them not answering emails.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: Which is why we start it now.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Sorry, my headphones just died, one sec.

turns.speaker: Diego
turns.text: Classic Monday.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Can we run certification and refunds in parallel? Or is that the same people?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Look, it's mostly me on both.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: Then we need someone else on certification.

turns.speaker: Diego
turns.text: I could do certification? I'd need someone to walk me through it first.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: The first time takes ages. There's a lot of tribal knowledge.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Does anyone else here actually know the cert process end to end? Because if it's just—

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: My bigger worry is test coverage. We're at eighty percent on payments, and that's not enough for a new API.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: Eighty sounds fine to me.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Coverage aside, I hear refunds first. Does anyone object?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: I object a little. I want the ledger refactor in this sprint, even half of it.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: Half a refactor is how you get two ledgers.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's, okay, that's actually a fair point.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: So the ranking is refunds, then certification, then the ledger work if there's room.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: If there's room. Which there won't be.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: There's never room. That's my point.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Okay, capacity. We're six engineers, but two of you aren't here today.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And Hannah's out the second week, right?

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Right. PTO next sprint is seven person-days total.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: Seven days is a lot. That's almost a whole person.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And on-call ate half a person last sprint. Eleven pages.

turns.speaker: Diego
turns.text: Eleven? It felt like more.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: It felt like a hundred. I got paged during my kid's recital.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Okay. What velocity do we plan to?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Our three-sprint average is thirty-eight.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Then with the PTO, I'd plan to thirty, maybe thirty-two.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: Thirty doesn't fit refunds and certification.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Then something doesn't fit. Let's be honest about it now, not in two weeks.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: Has anyone actually told the partner we might be short-staffed?

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Good question. Let's come back to that one.

turns.speaker: Diego
turns.text: Sorry, quick one, is anyone watering the plant by the window? It's looking really sad.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That plant has been dying since March. It's a lifestyle at this point.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: I watered it last week! I think it's the radiator, it's right next to it.

turns.speaker: Diego
turns.text: I read that they like being talked to. Maybe it's lonely.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Okay, nobody's adopting the plant in sprint planning. Capacity.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Realistically, I can't be on refunds, certification and on-call at the same time.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Then you're off the on-call rotation this sprint. Diego shadows Priyanka on-call instead. Done.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Thank you. Seriously.

turns.speaker: Diego
turns.text: Shadow on-call. Okay. That's, okay.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Diego, could you pair with Marcus on certification for the first week, so the knowledge isn't just in one head?

turns.speaker: Diego
turns.text: Yeah, I'll take the cert onboarding with Marcus, starting Monday.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: I'll write up the cert steps as we go, so it's not tribal anymore.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: And the status page ticket?

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Status page is probably the first thing to drop if refunds slip.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: That's fair.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Last one, risks. What keeps you up at night?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: The two open security findings on payments. They're not critical, but they're old.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: Are they blocking the partner launch?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Not technically. But if the partner's security team asks, it looks bad.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Can someone own getting those two closed this sprint?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: I'd love to, but you just saw my sprint.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: It would be good if someone from platform took a look at them.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: I'll raise the security findings with the platform lead on Thursday and ask for an owner.

turns.speaker: Diego
turns.text: What happens if the bank certification fails the first time? Do we just get another window?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good question.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: You get another window, but it's another three weeks of waiting.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: That's the real risk then. If cert slips, the partner date slips.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: The refund date is fixed, though. The partner announced it.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And our success rate is only ninety-seven point eight right now, so I'd rather not rush anything that touches money.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Agreed. I want a weekly check on cert progress, every Wednesday, for the whole sprint. That's decided.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: Fine by me.

turns.speaker: Diego
turns.text: Should I put that on the calendar?

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Please. Thank you, Diego.

turns.speaker: Diego
turns.text: Okay, I'll send the invite for the Wednesday cert check today.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Okay, team. That's the plan. Let's be honest in standup if it starts slipping. Thanks all.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Thanks.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: Thanks, everyone.
